summary:
BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Fluidstack is the tenant-of-record, not the owner, of roughly 1.4 GW of contracted critical IT load across five US campuses being built for Anthropic — Lake Mariner NY (378 MW, TeraWulf), Abernathy TX (168 MW, the joint venture it now controls), Barber Lake TX (207 MW, Cipher), River Bend LA (245 MW, Hut 8) and New Lebanon IN (430 MW, Meridian Arc) — and every one of those leases is bankable only because Google stands behind Fluidstack's rent with more than USD 6 billion of backstops and guarantees, paid for with penny warrants in two of the landlords; its own equity is USD 2.6 billion of total funding, USD 830 million of it a January 2026 Series A at a USD 7.5 billion valuation, plus a reported but unannounced USD 1.5 billion round at USD 18 billion in September 2026.

BACKGROUND. Founded in 2017 at Oxford by Gary Wu, César Maklary and Jamie Cox as a GPU marketplace, Fluidstack ran H100/H200 clusters for Mistral, Poolside, Black Forest Labs and Character.AI in third-party European colocation, financed GPUs through a Macquarie senior facility secured on the chips (April 2025), and signed a €10 billion, 1 GW French campus memorandum at the AI Action Summit (February 2025) that it abandoned in March 2026 as it pivoted to the United States. From August 2025 it became the intermediary tenant in a chain of former bitcoin miners' campuses, was named by Anthropic on 12 November 2025 as the builder of a USD 50 billion programme of custom data centres in Texas and New York, moved its headquarters to New York in December 2025, and in July 2026 bought TeraWulf's 50.1% of the Abernathy joint venture for about USD 530 million — its first owned campus. The 2026 website describes the company as building 'civilization-scale infrastructure for AI' and delivering 'gigawatts of compute in 6 months'; the company publishes no revenue, backlog or headcount, and its 2025 GPU-cloud marketing site has been taken down.
ecosystemRole: The clearest case in the corpus of the credit-substitution layer between a frontier lab and the power landlords: TeraWulf, Cipher and Hut 8 sign 10–25-year leases with a Fluidstack subsidiary, Google's recognition agreements make Google the tenant of last resort, and the end user — Anthropic — is named by the landlords only in separate partnership releases or not at all. For the ecosystem's utilities and vendors Fluidstack is the counterparty of record at Lake Mariner (NYPA/NYSEG hydro allocation), Abernathy (SPS territory), Barber Lake (AEP Texas/ERCOT), River Bend (Entergy Louisiana, 330 MW utility capacity), New Lebanon (Hoosier Energy/WIN Energy co-ops) and now Wythe County, Virginia (Appalachian Power's large-load list) and Okmulgee, Oklahoma (AEP-PSO, Jane Street as first tenant).

productsAndServices.name: Data-centre development and operations for frontier labs (the tenant-operator model)
productsAndServices.description: Fluidstack's 2026 business: it secures power and sites, signs the lease as tenant, specifies the liquid-cooled halls the landlord builds, procures and racks the compute, and operates the clusters for a single end user — 'power acquisition, data center design, construction, and operations' in the company's words. The buildings belong to the landlord (TeraWulf, Cipher, Hut 8, Meridian Arc) and the chips increasingly to a financing vehicle; Fluidstack sells speed.
highlights: Home page (2026): 'We build technology to enable delivery of gigawatts of compute in 6 months rather than the industry's 18-24 months'; jobs page: 'We build gigawatt-scale data centers from the ground up, delivered in months'.

Anthropic (12 November 2025) chose Fluidstack 'for its ability to move with exceptional agility, enabling rapid delivery of gigawatts of power'; the programme is 'USD 50 billion' of 'custom-built data centers designed specifically for Anthropic's workloads' in Texas and New York, 'with additional sites planned', 'approximately 800 permanent jobs and 2,400 construction jobs', sites 'expected to come online throughout 2026'.

Contracted lease positions per the landlords' filings: Lake Mariner NY 378 MW critical IT (three 10-year leases, ~USD 6.7 billion initial term); Abernathy TX 168 MW (25-year hosting term, ~USD 9.5 billion); Barber Lake TX 207 MW (10-year, ~USD 3.8 billion); River Bend LA 245 MW (15-year triple-net, USD 7.0 billion); New Lebanon IN 430 MW (15-year master lease behind USD 5.7 billion of Meridian Arc notes).

SemiAnalysis ClusterMAX 2.0 (November 2025, Gold tier, one of six among 84 providers): Fluidstack has 'the most unique business model' and is 'effectively the hired gun that organizations go to in order to turn bronze-tier datacenter infrastructure into a gold-tier customer experience'; 'the speed at which the Fluidstack team addressed issues was unmatched in all our testing'.

First-party project sites for owned developments: Sullivan County, Indiana ('a USD 65 billion development', 2027 start, leased 'exclusively to American tenants', USD 50 million of community payments) and Okmulgee, Oklahoma (first phase September 2027, final September 2028, Jane Street as first tenant, AEP-PSO power, 'Fluidstack is paying for all of the energy and energy infrastructure').
productsAndServices.positioning: Against CoreWeave, Nebius, Lambda and Crusoe — which own or finance GPUs and, increasingly, buildings — Fluidstack owns almost nothing: measuredai's July 2026 analysis calls it 'the pure tenant-operator' that 'owns zero buildings across its five U.S. sites while managing operations through five bankruptcy-remote tenant SPVs'. Its differentiator is a Google credit wrap that no other neocloud carries; its weakness is that the same wrap makes it replaceable — Anthropic signed its 401 MW Kentucky lease with TeraWulf directly in July 2026 with no Fluidstack involvement.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct, single-tenant contracts with AI labs; leases signed by US subsidiaries (Fluidstack USA I/II/III Inc., Fluidstack CS I Inc.) with Google recognition agreements; the company says it enables labs 'to access cutting-edge compute without typical multi-year contracts', but the landlord leases behind it run 10–25 years.
targetSegments: Frontier AI labs (Anthropic, Meta, Mistral, Poolside, Black Forest Labs, Character.AI named by the company)
Quantitative finance (Jane Street as Okmulgee first tenant)
productsAndServices.roadmap: Sites 'coming online throughout 2026' (Anthropic release); Lake Mariner CB-3 energized July 2026, CB-4 phased delivery 2H 2026, CB-5 early 2027; Abernathy targeted Q4 2026; Barber Lake September 2026 and 39 MW by January 2027; River Bend first hall Q2 2027; New Lebanon first hall July 2027; Okmulgee September 2027; Sullivan County from 2027.

productsAndServices.name: Managed GPU cloud platform — Managed Kubernetes, Managed Slurm, Lighthouse, Atlas API and fluidctl
productsAndServices.description: The software Fluidstack runs on top of leased halls and financed GPUs: 'an AI cloud platform designed from the ground up to meet the security, reliability, and scale requirements of top AI labs', with bare-metal container and batch orchestration, DCGM-based health checks, auto-remediation and a management API whose host is api.atlas.fluidstack.io.
highlights: Managed Kubernetes: 'ultra-reliable bare metal container orchestration platform powering frontier model training and inference' with the NVIDIA GPU Operator and Network Operator, passive and active health checks and observability; provisioned through sales, not self-serve ('can not be provisioned via API').
Managed Slurm: bare-metal batch orchestration for 'frontier model training' with Pyxis/Enroot containers and 'topology-aware scheduling' to cut collective-communication latency.

Lighthouse: 'the monitoring, observability, and reliability suite' — managed Grafana dashboards, passive DCGM background checks (PCIe, memory, firmware, thermal, power, NVLink and NVSwitch errors), active DCGM checks ('~2 minutes per run', preview) and auto-remediation (preview) that will 'automatically drain, power-cycle, and schedule physical maintenance for nodes'.

Scale claim (2025 boilerplate): 'over 100,000 GPUs under management' and 'rapid access to high-performance exa-scale compute within days' for 'multi-thousand GPU workloads'. The GPU catalogue and price list that the 2025 site carried are gone; docs.atlas.fluidstack.io answered 503 on every attempt — collection gap.
Status page: 'All services are online', no incidents recorded May–July 2026; no regions or components are named.
productsAndServices.positioning: Comparable to the orchestration layers Lambda, Nebius and Nscale sell, but Fluidstack's is documented only for existing customers — there is no public pricing, region list or instance catalogue in 2026, which is consistent with a company that now sells whole campuses rather than hours.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Managed services inside single-tenant contracts; SSO or API credentials via fluidctl; Projects give 'logical and network isolation'.
targetSegments: AI labs running multi-thousand-GPU training and inference on Fluidstack-operated clusters
productsAndServices.roadmap: Active DCGM checks and auto-remediation are 'preview' features (docs, 2026).

productsAndServices.name: European GPU clusters — Iceland/Nordics with Borealis, Dell and NVIDIA; the cancelled Mistral/Eclairion and Bosquel projects
productsAndServices.description: The 2025 European business: NVIDIA HGX H200 clusters on Dell PowerEdge XE9680 with Quantum-2 InfiniBand in Borealis Data Center's Icelandic sites on hydro and geothermal power, a planned 18,000-GPU Mistral AI supercomputer with Eclairion at Bruyères-le-Châtel, and the 1 GW nuclear-powered Bosquel campus — the last two dropped in March 2026.
highlights: 25 March 2025: 'deploying and managing Exascale clusters across Iceland and Europe' with Borealis, Dell and NVIDIA on '100% renewable energy (hydro and geothermal)'; Poolside's CEO: 'Fluidstack's speed, reliability, and customer support are second to none'.

3 March 2025: 'Fluidstack Delivering Europe's Largest AI Supercomputer to Mistral AI in 2025' — '>18,000 GPUs' with Eclairion, first tranche 'operational by Summer 2025' on '100% decarbonized electricity'. Bloomberg (18 March 2026) reported the Eclairion deal cancelled; the release has been removed from the company's site.

10 February 2025: memorandum with the French government (ministers Lombard and Feracci, signed by Maklary) for 'up to 1 gigawatt (GW) of dedicated AI compute power', 'predominantly nuclear energy', a '€10 billion' first phase, 'close to 500,000 next-generation AI chips', live 2026 and 'beyond 1 GW by 2028'. Abandoned March 2026 per Bloomberg and the French economy ministry; the Somme authorities and RTE reopened the site to other investors.
Iceland capacity is what the Macquarie facility financed: 'a senior debt facility secured by NVIDIA GPUs', GPUs 'deployed' in an Icelandic data centre, closed 'in a matter of weeks' (Macquarie).
UK Companies House lists Fluidstack Iceland/Norway/Finland Holdings I Ltd and Fluidstack France Holdings I Ltd (2025) — residual Nordic activity; no UK or Norwegian project has been announced.
productsAndServices.positioning: Fluidstack was the French state's chosen sovereign-compute partner for one year; Julien Simon's critique is that it became redundant 'when Mistral and Nvidia connected directly'. Nscale (Narvik, Loughton, Sines) now holds the European sovereign-neocloud position Fluidstack vacated.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Reserved clusters in third-party colocation; GPUs financed on Fluidstack's own balance sheet via asset-backed debt.
targetSegments: European AI labs (Mistral, Poolside, Black Forest Labs)
productsAndServices.roadmap: No European roadmap is published in 2026.

productsAndServices.name: Power and land development — Sullivan County IN, Okmulgee OK, Wythe County VA, Harlingen TX
productsAndServices.description: From late 2025 Fluidstack began acquiring powered land and developing campuses in its own name rather than leasing from a landlord: a 2.1 GW-capable Indiana industrial park (with Meridian Arc/Next Frontier), a city-approved Oklahoma campus with Jane Street as first tenant, the 99-acre Solis Arx tract at Progress Park in Wythe County, Virginia, and a Harlingen, Texas site whose project page is not yet reachable.
highlights: New Lebanon, Sullivan County, Indiana: Meridian Arc HoldCo (Frontier Development Holdings/Next Frontier 50.1%, Fluidstack Ltd 49.9%) priced USD 5.7 billion of 6.25% senior secured notes due 2031 (April 2026, Fitch BB, Morgan Stanley) to buy about 140 acres and build 245 MW + 185 MW of critical IT '100% leased to Fluidstack over a 15-year base lease term', 'guaranteed by Google'; power through a multi-party agreement with Hoosier Energy and WIN Energy REMC; first hall July 2027.

Okmulgee, Oklahoma (company project site): first phase September 2027, final September 2028; 'Jane Street will be the first tenant'; AEP-PSO as power provider; 'Fluidstack is paying for all of the energy and energy infrastructure'; a USD 7 million education commitment; designed to comply with Oklahoma SB 259 (water) and the Data Center Consumer Ratepayer Protection Act of 2026.

Wythe County, Virginia: the county's project page records that Solis Arx's campus was 'announced on December 5, 2025' on a '99-acre tract within Progress Park' and that 'on June 9, 2026, a representative of Fluidstack presented to the Board of Supervisors regarding the acquisition of Solis Arx'; Appalachian Power's large-load list (Cardinal News, 31 July 2026) carries 'Fluidstack (formerly Solis Arx) — Unknown MW — Wythe — In progress'.

Sullivan County project site: 'a USD 65 billion development', 'no property-tax incentives sought', '100% Self-Funded Energy', closed-loop cooling, a 55 dB noise limit; the company's public-affairs representative cited 'nearly USD 600 million in labor contracts' at the August 2026 open house.
productsAndServices.positioning: This is the step from tenant to developer that Crusoe, Nscale and (through Justified) TeraWulf's own tenants have taken; Fluidstack's version keeps a financial partner (Coatue-linked Next Frontier at New Lebanon) as majority owner and Google as guarantor.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Long-term single-tenant leases; project bonds at the holding-company level.
productsAndServices.roadmap: New Lebanon capacity from late 2026, first hall July 2027; Okmulgee September 2027 and September 2028; Wythe County and Harlingen undated.

productsAndServices.name: GPU and capacity financing — Macquarie asset-backed facility, capacity purchases from smaller neoclouds, the Broadcom–Apollo–Blackstone chip vehicle
productsAndServices.description: The capital side of the model: GPUs financed against themselves (Macquarie, 2025), GPU capacity bought in from smaller providers when needed (a two-year, USD 127 million contract with Boost Run, December 2025), and, for the Anthropic sites, TPUs bought by a special-purpose vehicle and leased to Anthropic rather than to Fluidstack (the Broadcom–Apollo–Blackstone platform, June 2026, reported at about USD 35 billion for the first tranche).
highlights: Macquarie (1 April 2025): 'strategic GPU financing deal to supply GPUs to premier AI research labs across Europe'; 'The financing structure, secured by the GPUs themselves, allows Fluidstack to provide AI compute to customers…without the burden of long-term commitments'; the amount is not stated by either party (press: up to USD 10 billion of capacity).

Boost Run (SPAC 8-K, 15 December 2025): 'Fluidstack, a leading AI cloud platform, has entered into a two-year USD 127 million contract with Boost Run to facilitate inference and training clusters for customers within its world-class portfolio' — Fluidstack as buyer of capacity.

Broadcom–Apollo–Blackstone (June 2026, press summaries; the Broadcom release page was unreachable): an initial USD 35 billion tranche 'to facilitate 1GW of compute infrastructure Anthropic is expected to deploy in Fluidstack-based sites, starting in mid-2026'; the vehicle buys the chips — including Google TPUs — and leases them to Anthropic, with Broadcom supporting residual value. measuredai reported the first TPU capacity live at Lake Mariner on 5 July 2026.
Destiny Tech100's prospectus (August 2026) describes the company as 'securing power, data center capacity, and financing through long-term partnerships rather than owning infrastructure outright'.
productsAndServices.positioning: Where CoreWeave and Lambda pledge owned GPUs to lenders, Fluidstack's US model puts the chips in a lessor vehicle and the credit on Google — Dave Friedman's February 2026 line: 'The collateral is cosmetic. The credit is Google's.'
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Not a product sold; structures behind the contracts.
targetSegments: Lenders and lessors (Macquarie, Apollo, Blackstone, project bondholders)
productsAndServices.roadmap: Bloomberg reported (September 2026) that Blackstone was weighing a second debt package for the Anthropic chip deal.

relationships.context:
Anthropic's release: 'building data centers with Fluidstack in Texas and New York, with more sites to come', chosen 'for its ability to move with exceptional agility, enabling rapid delivery of gigawatts of power'; Fluidstack's Gary Wu: 'Fluidstack was built for this moment.' The sites are not named by either party. Hut 8's release of 17 December 2025 is the one landlord document that closes the loop: 'at least 245 megawatts and up to 2,295 MW of AI data center infrastructure for Anthropic, leveraging clusters operated by Fluidstack', with Anthropic's Head of Compute James Bradbury quoted.

TeraWulf and Cipher describe the end user only as 'a global hyperscale AI platform developing frontier-scale foundation models'. In July 2026 Anthropic signed its 401 MW Hawesville, Kentucky lease with TeraWulf directly — Fluidstack is not a party — and in August 2026 it contracted with Nscale, Lambda and Riot as well; Fluidstack is one channel among several.

relationships.scale: > USD 6 billion of lease backstops and guarantees; warrants ~14% of TeraWulf and ~5.4% of Cipher
relationships.note: Google backstops Fluidstack's lease obligations at every US campus — USD 3.2 billion at Lake Mariner, USD 1.3 billion at Abernathy, USD 1.73 billion at Barber Lake, the full 15-year River Bend base term, and the New Lebanon master lease — and holds penny warrants in TeraWulf and Cipher in return.
relationships.context:
The mechanics are in the landlords' 8-Ks: Google LLC signs a recognition agreement per building; on 'a payment default under a Fluidstack Lease, or if Fluidstack becomes subject to an insolvency event' Google may pay the termination fee or 'pay all rent currently due under the Fluidstack Lease and assume the Fluidstack Lease as the tenant'. The backstop becomes effective at lease commencement — TeraWulf's Q2 2026 release records USD 600 million of it switching on when CB-3 was delivered. Cipher carries a USD 544.5 million asset for 'the value of Google agreeing to make the lease payments from Fluidstack'.

Google has never published a page naming Fluidstack; Fluidstack's one joint release calls it 'a leading global hyperscale partner'. The Wall Street Journal reported (February 2026) that Google was exploring a USD 100 million equity investment in Fluidstack tied to TPU distribution, and the TPUs Anthropic runs at Fluidstack sites are, per press accounts of the Broadcom–Apollo–Blackstone vehicle, Google-built chips leased to Anthropic.

strategyRead: 1. **(High confidence)** We assess that Fluidstack's product is credit substitution plus speed, not compute. Basis: every US lease is signed by a bankruptcy-remote Fluidstack subsidiary and every one carries a Google recognition agreement under which Google may 'assume the Fluidstack Lease as the tenant'; TeraWulf's 10-K calls that support 'a key factor in enabling efficient financing'; Cipher books it as a USD 544.5 million asset; the company's own 2026 site sells 'gigawatts of compute in 6 months'. About USD 27 billion of base-term rent stands on roughly USD 2.6 billion of equity.

2. **(High confidence)** We assess that the tenant-of-record position is replaceable by its own customer, and that July 2026 showed it. Basis: Anthropic signed 401 MW at Hawesville directly with TeraWulf 'supported by an investment-grade credit', with no Fluidstack entity in the lease; Anthropic has since contracted directly or through other operators with Nscale, Lambda, Riot and Hut 8's Beacon Point. Fluidstack's answer — buying the Abernathy campus and developing Okmulgee, Sullivan County and Wythe County in its own name — is a move from tenant to owner-developer that its balance sheet has not yet been shown to carry.

3. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess that construction-period risk, not tenant credit, is where this chain can break. Basis: the backstop 'becomes effective as of the commencement date' (TeraWulf 10-Q), so bondholders at Flash Compute and Meridian Arc carry the build with only a capped USD 100 million completion guarantee; Quinn Emanuel notes that a delay beyond 180 days lets Fluidstack terminate 'and Google's backstop obligation would never trigger'. The schedule has already moved: CB-5 from '2H 2026' to 'early 2027', Abernathy from '2H 2026' to 'Q4 2026'. Barber Lake is reported on schedule.

4. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess that Google's position — guarantor of the leases, warrant-holder in two landlords, reported prospective shareholder in the tenant and, through the Broadcom–Apollo–Blackstone vehicle, the designer of the chips leased to the end user — makes the Fluidstack chain a Google TPU distribution channel to Anthropic as much as a neocloud. Basis: the landlords' 8-Ks, the WSJ-reported USD 100 million equity talks tied to Ironwood distribution, and press descriptions of the chip vehicle; Google has published nothing naming Fluidstack, so the mechanism is inferred from counterparties' filings.

5. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess that the European withdrawal was a choice of counterparty quality over sovereignty. Basis: the French memorandum was a non-binding MoU with no anchor tenant; the US leases have a AA+ guarantor and a single frontier lab behind them; Bloomberg's account and the HQ move to New York point the same way. The reputational cost is real — the Somme authorities had to re-tender — and it is the reason a European government would now look to Nscale rather than Fluidstack.

Basis: the 2026 home page names Anthropic, NVIDIA and Meta; Jane Street is the only other named tenant (Okmulgee, first phase September 2027); trade press maps all five leased campuses to the Anthropic programme. The company's 2025 customer list (Mistral, Poolside, Black Forest Labs, Character.AI) belongs to the European business it wound down. Concentration is inferred, not stated.

Collection gaps: Fluidstack has never published revenue, backlog, headcount or a lease; the 2025 GPU-cloud site (pricing, GPU catalogue, solutions pages) has been removed and the Atlas documentation host was unreachable; fluidstack.io carries no leadership page and no headshots; Google has never named Fluidstack; the Broadcom chip-vehicle release and several Bloomberg, DCD and Forbes pages were unreachable and are cited from reprints or search summaries; Fluidstack Ltd's filed FY2024 accounts were not read; the France withdrawal has no first-party statement.
